instructions: Complete the notes below. Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.

items.heading: Chemistry of the dye
items.prompt: The living leaf is not blue; the colour forms from a colourless ____ once the leaves have been steeped and aerated.

evidence.quote: the pigment develops from a colourless precursor only when the crushed foliage

items.how: Scan paragraph A for the sentence explaining how colour arises in the leaf. Underline the words colourless and steeped, then identify which noun the text uses for the substance that exists before the blue appears.
items.again: Re-read the sentence about chemistry and check that your word names the substance, not the process. Adjectives and verbs from the same sentence fit the grammar but do not name what exists in the leaf before steeping.

items.prompt: Woad yields the same pigment but only in much lower ____, so far more of it was required.

evidence.quote: yields the same molecule in far lower concentrations

items.how: Find the comparison between woad and indigo in paragraph A. Underline the phrase about quantity of plant material and look at the noun that follows the word lower, remembering that the notes use pigment where the text uses a synonym.
items.again: The notes paraphrase molecule as pigment, so match meaning, not wording. Check that your answer is plural, as the text has it, and that it describes proportion within the plant rather than the total harvest or price.

items.heading: Extraction
items.prompt: Harvested stems were held under water in a vat by means of heavy ____.

evidence.quote: held down with heavy timber for roughly a day

items.how: Move to paragraph B and follow the first stage of extraction. Underline the vat, the stems and the verb phrase that describes keeping them submerged, then read what material is named immediately afterwards.
items.again: Look at what is said to hold the stems down, not at what the labourers used later for beating. A distractor appears two sentences later in the form of paddles and wheels, which belong to a different vat and a different stage.

items.prompt: The finished cubes were dried slowly in ____ because sunlight was thought to damage them.

evidence.quote: dried slowly in shade because direct sunlight was believed to crack them

items.how: Scan paragraph B for the drying stage, which follows boiling, straining and pressing. Underline dried and sunlight in the notes, and find where the text states the condition under which drying took place.
items.again: Test your word by reading the sentence aloud with the notes wording. Check that it names a place or condition, not a tool. Boiling and pressing come first in the sequence, so ignore the earlier stages when choosing.

items.heading: Dyeing at Calloway
items.prompt: The vat had to be maintained in a steady, mildly ____ condition.

evidence.quote: kept in a steady and mildly alkaline state

items.how: Locate the Calloway account in paragraph C and find the sentence about looking after the vat itself. Underline steady and mildly, then read the adjective that follows them in the text.
items.again: Several adjectives describe the dye in paragraph C, including a colour term. Check that your choice describes the chemical state of the vat, not the colour of the liquid, by re-reading the sentence about the senior dyer.

items.heading: Synthetic competition
items.prompt: The product made by German chemists beat plantation dye on price and was more ____ in strength.

evidence.quote: Synthetic indigo was cheaper, more uniform in strength

items.how: Go to paragraph E and find the list of advantages claimed for the laboratory product. Underline cheaper and strength in the notes and look for the adjective that sits between them in the original.
items.again: The paragraph lists several advantages in a row, so match the one tied to strength. Check that the word fits grammatically before strength, and that you did not choose a quality attached to weather or to labour.

items.prompt: In traditional denim, only the ____ threads carry the dye, while the weft stays white.

evidence.quote: only the warp threads are dyed, while the weft remains white

items.how: Find the description of denim construction in paragraph F. Underline the contrast between two sets of threads in the notes, and read which set the text says is dyed.
items.again: The notes already give you the undyed set, so read the original contrast to see which of the two terms remains. Make sure you took the word from the correct side of the contrast and spelt it exactly as printed.
